newsitem.title: INDIA: India PM calls for mass movement against corruption.
newsitem.headline: India PM calls for mass movement against corruption.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Friday asked the people to launch a mass movement to stamp out corruption and isolate the corrupt.

"It (corruption) is eating into the country's vitals like termites," said Gujral, addressing the nation from the ramparts of the historic Red Fort on the 50th anniversary of India's independence from British rule.
Gujral, who devoted much of his 75-minute speech to the ills of graft, said Indians must start a non-cooperation movement along the lines of Mahatma Gandhi's "Satyagraha", or civil disobedience.
"Let us all resolve today that we would not give a single penny as a bribe to get our work done at any level," he said.
Gujral's reference to corruption comes at a time when Indian courts are dealing with a large number of cases involving graft in high places.
"A bigger danger to this country today comes from those occupying top positions. They betray the country because of their greed for bribes," he said.
Laloo Prasad Yadav, a former leader of Gujral's Janata Dal party, has been indicted in a $280-million scandal in Bihar state. Yadav says he is innocent.
Former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao of the Congress party has been indicted in two criminal corruption cases. He also denies any wrongdoing.
Gujral said if the country's enemies attacked it from outside, India's soldiers could meet the challenge.
"But if some one betrays the country from within, takes bribes, he becomes a threat to the nation," he said.

"Our war against corruption is honest and candid," he said. "And for this, we have to build a mass movement, in which all can join so that corruption in politics, politicians and public life must end."
"This disease has gone very far. Be it in government purchases, or matters of tax or customs, some people are under the impression that corruption is their birth right," he said.
"I am warning them. I assure you that the long arm of the law will be further strengthened so that the corrupt cannot escape," Gujral said.
Gujral also expressed concern over criminals entering politics in growing numbers.
"Corruption in India has also assumed a different form -- the nexus between criminals and politics. To stamp it out, we must all join hands. The government alone cannot do it," he said.
Gujral called for reforms to the electoral system to stamp out money politics.

He also said the defence ministry had set a committee to see that its purchases were transparent. Similar committees, comprising men of integrity, would be set up by other ministries as well, Gujral said.
"There will not be any kickbacks. Everything will be transparent," he said.
